criteria.criterion: A backtest test builds fixture records with the verbatim text and timestamps of kn3q (2026-10-13T15:07:02Z), qk2d (16:20:49Z) and ar1x (19:21:56Z), with D87 starting 2026-10-13T19:21Z. D87 is under review citing only ar1x, directly and through its derived record. kn3q and qk2d are not cited. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: The test with_the_real_interventions_d87_is_under_review_citing_only_ar1x passed. kn3q and ar1x match the request's text exactly once the runtime-built word "Operator" is filled in, and all three times match. D87 starts at 2026-10-13T19:21:00Z. The only derived record is ar1x. D87's single citation names ar1x and its derived record, and every derived citation has record and source both equal to ar1x. Neither the report nor D87's citations mention kn3q or qk2d. qk2d's text is a disclosed placeholder (see findings).

criteria.criterion: Unit tests: 'GitHub refused a merge commit (HTTP 405)' and 'Operator squash-merged PR #41 by hand ... after GitHub refused a merge commit (HTTP 405).' derive a merge refusal. kn3q's text derives nothing. 'I merged by hand because the push failed with HTTP 422' and 'the push failed with HTTP 422' derive nothing. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: watcher::tests::the_code_must_be_tied_to_the_refusal_of_the_merge passed. It asserts each of the listed cases, including the full ar1x and kn3q texts.

criteria.criterion: The refusal derivation requires the HTTP code to be tied to the refusal of the merge itself, for example 'refused a merge ... (HTTP 405)'. A bare 'merged' elsewhere in the text is not enough.
criteria.evidence: In watcher.rs, `refused_merge_code` needs the whole word `refused`, optional determiners, the whole word `merge`, then `HTTP <code>` within four words and before `;`, a line break or a sentence end. `names_merge` is removed, and `derive_host_error` uses only `refused_merge_code`.

criteria.criterion: A decision's start time comes from the first commit that introduced its id heading ('## D87 '), not from its current full heading text. The code finds that commit with git history, and a test or code path shows that a renamed heading still dates from the first commit.
criteria.evidence: `decision_start` runs `git log --reverse --format=%cI -S "## <id> " -- docs/decisions.md` and takes the first line. The test a_decision_is_dated_from_the_first_commit_that_added_its_id_heading commits D87, then renames its heading. The start stays at the first commit (19:21), and an unknown id gives None. The test passed. `run()` now calls `starts_from_history`, and `athena backtest` ran on this tree without a dating error.

criteria.criterion: The backtest counts only records after the decision's start. It validates each cited record against the signal's fields and time window, and fails when any citation is invalid. A test with a pre-start cited record fails the backtest. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: `run_signals` drops records at or before the start via `after_start`. `validate_citations` checks each cited record: it exists, matches the signal, falls after the start, and a derived record's source intervention exists and falls after the start. `run_on_from` adds these findings, so any invalid citation fails the report. Three tests passed: the pre-start test (one refusal at 15:08 is left out; citing it gives an (e) 'not later than' finding), and the test for citations of missing records.

criteria.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena ran fmt, clippy with -D warnings, and cargo test (434 tests); all passed. I re-ran the backtest and watcher suites and they passed.

criteria.criterion: The clause splitting no longer breaks on decimal points or version numbers, or the derivation does not depend on it.
criteria.evidence: A full stop ends the clause only when whitespace or the end of the text follows it. The test a_version_number_does_not_cut_the_clause covers 'GitHub 3.1 refused…' and 'in v1.2 (HTTP 405)', and checks that a real sentence end still cuts the clause. It passed.

findings.summary: qk2d's fixture text is a placeholder, not the real intervention text.
findings.evidence: The doc comment says 'The text of qk2d is a stand-in with no refusal in it', and the fixture uses 'Edited the landing summary by hand.'. The request gave only qk2d's time, and the repository holds no qk2d text: docs/design/decision-sets.md:511 says only 'An intervention of class `code`'. qk2d falls before D87's start, so it is excluded either way. Once the real records are available, its fixture text should be checked against them.

findings.summary: Fixture job ids and the 'why' text are made up.
findings.evidence: The job ids for the vbdn and qk2d interventions (20261013-140000-vbdn, 20261013-160000-qk2j) and the 'why' field 'recorded after the fact' do not come from the real records. This does not affect the criteria.

summary: The change does what the request asks. `derive_host_error` now derives a refusal only when an `HTTP <code>` follows "refused [a/the/to/any] merge" within four words and before the clause ends, so "the push failed with HTTP 422" and kn3q's text derive nothing. A full stop inside a decimal or version number no longer ends the clause. Each decision now starts at the first commit that added its id heading: `git log --reverse -S "## <id> "`. A test commits a heading and then renames it, and the start still comes from the first commit. The backtest counts only records later than that start. It checks every cited record against the signal's fields and the time window, and any invalid citation is a condition (e) finding that fails the run. I ran the backtest and watcher test suites (all passed) and `athena backtest` on this tree; the start lookup ran against real git history without an error. One minor gap: qk2d's text in the fixture is a placeholder. The request gave only its time, and its text is nowhere in this repository.
